intro: The excavators broke the seal on a tomb that appears on no dynasty list, and the air that came out smelled of cedar resin and ancient dust. Every chamber is empty except for a single inscription, carved in a script that borrows the familiar signs and then breaks their rules. At the far end of the main hall stands a cedar shelving unit whose pigeonholes are cut as if for one thing alone: the shallow boxes fit the short finds, the deep ones the long, and none will hold two. The finds are laid in as the lamplight fades, each in the only hole that closes neatly around it, and the men watch the smoke-black backs of the occupied niches in the order the holes stand. The last word of the dig is not in the inscription but in that soot, read along the row.
echo: What walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon and three in the evening?

puzzles.title: Field Of Reeds
puzzles.flavor: Every row inside the tomb holds one of everything. So does every column, and every box. Then read the numbered squares.
hints: Sudoku using the letters shown instead of digits (each row, column and box uses each letter once). Read the numbered squares in order.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with L.

puzzles.title: Cartouche
puzzles.flavor: Unjumble the kit list. You'll have one letter left over every time, and you'll want to keep those.
hints: Each jumble is an anagram of a word from this round's theme plus one extra letter. The extra letters, in order, spell the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with A.

puzzles.title: Hall Of Records
puzzles.flavor: The host inside the tomb fussed over the seating plan for days. Every guest pays for their chair with one letter of their name: the further along the row, the deeper into the name.

clues: Gemma sits somewhere between Phineas and Raphael.
Phineas sits somewhere between Gemma and Magnus.
Gemma and Valentine sit side by side.
Valentine sits immediately to the right of Raphael.
Exactly 2 people sit between Phineas and Valentine.

hints: A logic puzzle: use the clues to find the one seating that works (seats are numbered 1 to n from the left). Then the guest in seat k gives the k-th letter of their name.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with R.

puzzles.title: Canopic Jars
puzzles.flavor: A mosaic inside the tomb was taken apart tile by tile, and all that was kept was the count of each run.
hints: A nonogram (paint-by-numbers). The filled picture is the answer written in 5×5 block letters.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with S.

puzzles.title: Solar Barque
puzzles.flavor: Someone wrote this out in a zigzag across three lines of the ledger, then copied each line out in turn.

blocks.text: EYDTS HNWAH RUTMS EIGHV RGOHN EDWTA IGEOD NTEOD OWNFO TIPGI HEOLP EOUNI SLRDW YARHA SRY

hints: Rail-fence transposition of a sentence with the spaces removed. Try 2 to 5 rails; the sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with H.

puzzles.title: The Inundation
puzzles.flavor: Start in a corner, follow the edge, and keep turning inward. Which corner, and which way, is up to you to find.
hints: A sentence was written into the grid along a spiral, starting in one corner and winding inward. Find the corner and the direction, read the sentence (dots are padding), and it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

meta.title: Meta: Valley Of The Kings
meta.flavor: Pigeonholes, each cut to fit one thing, and some of them marked.
hints: Each answer fits exactly one row of the grid by length; the shaded squares, top to bottom, spell the final answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with S.
